name: Pinochle
tagline: Bid, pass cards with your partner, show your meld and take the counters.
rulesSummary: Partners sit across. Score meld and counters; first side to 1500 wins (both past it: the bidding side wins).
48 cards: two each of A 10 K Q J 9 in every suit, ranked in that order (the 10 beats the king). 12 cards each.
Bid in tens from 250; once you pass you're out. If the other three pass, the dealer is stuck at 250. The winner names trumps, gets 4 cards from their partner and passes 4 back.
Meld in trumps: run (A 10 K Q J) 150, with an extra K or Q 190, with both 230, double run 1500; royal marriage (K Q) 40; each 9 (dix) 10.
Any suit: marriage (K Q) 20; pinochle (Q♠ J♦) 40, double 300; one of each suit: aces 100, kings 80, queens 60, jacks 40 (two of each: ×10). A card can count in melds of different kinds.
If the bidders' meld plus all 250 trick points can't reach the bid, they're set at once. The bidder may also throw it in: lose the bid, and the other side scores its meld.
The bidder leads. Follow suit and beat the winning card if you can; if you can't follow, trump — higher than any trump already played, if you can.
Aces, 10s and kings taken are 10 each, the last trick 10 more. Bidders who reach the bid score meld plus points; fall short and lose the bid.
The other side scores its points, but keeps its meld only if it takes a counter or the last trick (a meld of only dix always counts).
